outcome: No result found addressing whether wild knots have infinitely many quadrisecants; the conjecture (attributed to Kuperberg, 1994) remains open exactly as stated in the frozen Wikipedia revision.
summary: I ran a broad set of searches for the wild-knot quadrisecant conjecture (that every wild knot has infinitely many quadrisecants, attributed to Kuperberg 1994) and found nothing addressing it in the window 26 Jan 2024 – present. The current live Wikipedia 'Quadrisecant' article still lists it as an unsolved problem with no update beyond the original attribution. Adjacent, pre-2024 background that repeatedly surfaced in searches — Kuperberg's theorem that every nontrivial tame knot has at least one quadrisecant, Denne's alternating-quadrisecant results for tame knots, the disproved 'quadrisecant approximation conjecture' (Denne/Sullivan et al., pre-2024), and the fact that every wild *arc* (not closed wild knot) has infinitely many quadrisecants — are all related-but-distinct results that predate the window or concern a different object (tame knots, or open arcs rather than closed wild knots), so none of them are cases of, or changes to, this specific bullet per §3.1. I also found genuine 2024-2026 wild-knot research — 'Knots Inside Fractals' (arXiv:2409.03639, Sep 2024) and 'Wild knots embedded in the Menger sponge' (arXiv:2602.20384, Feb 2026) — which construct new families of wild knots (in fractal/Menger-sponge settings) but do not mention quadrisecants at all; these are related problems (existence/classification of wild knots), not results on this conjecture. I found no preprint, announcement, or digestion — human or AI-assisted — that proves, disproves, or partially settles the infinitely-many-quadrisecants question for wild knots. I agree with the triage verdict of 'none': this is a case where nothing happened.
competing_reading: None of the adjacent results plausibly count as a case or partial resolution: the wild-arc quadrisecant result concerns arcs, not closed wild knots, and appears to predate 2024 in any case (it circulates as background in older quadrisecant literature, e.g. Denne's survey work), so even if it were on-topic it would be open_stale rather than a change within the window. I found no evidence it was newly proved or newly publicized in the window.
what_would_settle_it: A paper or announcement explicitly proving or disproving that every wild knot (as a closed curve, not an arc) has infinitely many quadrisecants, or exhibiting a wild knot with only finitely many quadrisecants as a counterexample.
